1

Details

Reach = the X17/IPC(E1) ratio a 50-day run detects at 3σ (Asimov over the θ histogram summed over E_n: a DC beam has no TOF tag). X17 counted only from E_n ≤ 2.75 MeV (E* ≤ 22 MeV, ATOMKI-like); counted at every E*, the NFS convention: 5.2×10⁻⁴. 14 days: 1.6×10⁻³.

The model's beam: ENDF/B-VIII.0 p + ⁹Be (LA150) through a Bethe slowing-down, checked against two published yields to 1 %.

Files: bepn_cyclotron/FEASIBILITY.md, FACILITY.md, bepn_beam.py, bepn_reach.py.

NPI Řež: the one bare, open-access Be converter at high current

the facilities this study compares; hover the dots and dotted terms for details

NPI CAS, Řež (near Prague, CZ)

Laboratory of Fast Neutron Generators: fast-neutron data for IFMIF-DONES, ITER, DEMO. Open access via CANAM.

TR-24: 18–24 MeV, 300 µA on a bare Be disk

High-power converter, 7.2 kW, forward-open: 2×10¹³ n/s at 18 MeV. U-120M (≤ 37 MeV, 35 µA) has a collimated beam today.

Status: converter (ask)

“Not operational yet” in 2019; prototype tested at 24 MeV in 2020. The BNCT HM-30s (30 MeV, 1 mA, Japan) are all moderated.

2

Details

Candidates (FACILITY.md §1): Sumitomo HM-30 BNCT cyclotrons (KURNS C-BENS, Southern Tohoku, Kansai BNCT) give 30 MeV at 1 mA but bury the Be in a Pb/Fe/Al/CaF₂ moderator for epithermal beams; KURNS plans to open C-BENS to fundamental research after KUR's shutdown (May 2026), so a fast port is worth asking about. Atomki's MGC-20E and TENMAK's 30 MeV cyclotron are µA-class.

NPI: TR-24 (ACSI, commissioned 2015) and U-120M (K = 40). Contacts (public): M. Majerle, M. Štefánik (fast neutron generators), J. Štursa (cyclotrons).

3

Details

TR-24: H⁻ multi-cusp source, stripping-foil extraction (energy set by the foil radius), two simultaneous beams; output 2 runs through a beamline and switching magnet to three target positions. High-power Be converter (CANAM): static Be disk 4 mm × Ø40 mm, ≤ 7.2 kW (0.9–3.5 kW/cm²), submerged-jet cooling, samples 20 mm from the target, ~2–3×10¹² n/cm²/s on axis.

Through a Ø8 cm collimator 2 m downstream at 0°, 18 MeV, 0.3 mA: 4.8e+09 n/s (bepn_beam.py).

The U-120M thick-Be station already has the X17 geometry: a collimator in movable shielding doors (Ø3–25 cm), the beam into the adjacent hall, a 15 m flight path to a dump. At 35 µA of 18 MeV H⁻/p and the cell at 3 m: 2.8×10⁻³.

The soft half is evaporation and ⁹Be break-up, nearly isotropic. The hard half is the (p,n) continuum: forward-peaked, but its 3–10 MeV bulk is there at 130° too.

18 MeV removes everything above 16 MeV, which is what makes the correlated background.

4

Details

Anchors (out/bepn_anchors.csv): 16 MeV y0_above_0.4: model/reference 0.99; 24 MeV y0: model/reference 1.49; 30 MeV ytot: model/reference 0.99. NPI's "5×10¹² n/s/sr forward" at 24 MeV, 0.3 mA matches the model at 30–40°, not at 0°.

The peaks at ~1.5 and ~6 MeV are the evaluation's MT 5 tables (sequential decay through ⁹B/⁸Be states); measured thick-target spectra (Brede 1989; NPI TOF, Majerle 2023) are smoother. The fractions above and below 2.75 MeV are what matter, and they move little.

Below 2.75 MeV: NPI TR-24, 18 MeV, 0° (baseline) 43 %, NPI TR-24, 24 MeV, 130° 40 %, HM-30, 30 MeV, 0° 31 %, Birmingham ⁷Li(p,n), 2.8 MeV 100 %, GANIL NFS d(40)+Be 2 %.

A single = a trigger leg (SiPM + back plastic) with a Micromegas segment in the active area.

Here, at full current: 9,146 singles and 287,300 legs per arm per second.

Random two-arm triggers ~10⁴/s; at the best throttle (0.63) DREAM is live 0.45.

5

Details

Legs need half a MIP (1.7 MeV) in the back plastic; proton recoils from fast neutrons give them freely, most without a Micromegas segment (legs/singles ≈ 30 here, against ≈ 7 at Birmingham).

Above 20 MeV (24 MeV at θ < 45°, the HM-30) the NFS forced run N4 is used; it has no leg tables, so its legs are its singles × 10.3 (N5's leg/single ratio at 10–20 MeV). At 18 MeV nothing is above 16.3 MeV and N5 alone carries the result.

More beam stops helping at ~2×10⁹ n/s on the cell: the DAQ, not the source, sets the reach

At 24 MeV, 0° and on the 30 MeV HM-30 the > 16 MeV tail adds correlated two-arm events (as at NFS): throttled ×6–40.

A 4× faster DAQ (5 samples): baseline 6.2×10⁻⁴ at full current.

A bigger machine does not help: the HM-30’s current goes into its tail.

Details

Best 50-day reach per configuration (big plastics, E* ≤ 22): NPI 18 MeV 0° 8.66×10⁻⁴; 18 MeV 130° 8.89×10⁻⁴; 24 MeV 130° 9.81×10⁻⁴; 24 MeV 0° 2.28×10⁻³; HM-30 130° 1.48×10⁻³; HM-30 0° 5.00×10⁻³; U-120M 35 µA, 3 m 2.80×10⁻³.

The DAQ variant (τ/4) is bepn_reach.py --tau-scale 0.25 --tag tau4 → out_tau4/.

X17 at the ATOMKI ratio is 0.8 % of the IPC in the window (Birmingham 1.9 %): half the IPC comes from E* > 22 MeV.

No correlated beam term at 18 MeV: the neutrons that make it (> 16 MeV) are absent.

7

Details

Window counts are for orientation; the reach uses the whole θ histogram. Accidentals: two singles from different particles within ±5 ns, from the source's own Geant4 singles, through the reconstruction. Correlated: same-event two-arm events, factorised.

8

Details

Unshielded: the 0° yield 3.8e+12 n/s/sr at 18 MeV, 0.3 mA, over (200 cm)², through one arm's 75 × 75 cm face.

Singles per neutron entering an arm are not simulated: 1–20 MeV neutrons make legs, so 10⁻⁴–10⁻³ (Birmingham used 10⁻⁶–10⁻⁴ for sub-MeV neutrons). Tenth-value layers are stand-ins (NCRP 144: ~40 cm concrete at 20–30 MeV). bepn_beam.shield() → out/bepn_shield.csv.

Against the other facilities: a pass, but ×2.6 behind Birmingham

Details

Contacts (public): M. Majerle, M. Štefánik (Laboratory of Fast Neutron Generators), J. Štursa (cyclotrons); FACILITY.md §5. KURNS (H. Tanaka): is there any way to run C-BENS with the moderator removed?

What this does not settle yet

Not in the simulation

• The wall, the room, the target backing and cooling water (a moderated component).

• The spectrum is the LA150 evaluation, checked on two integrals only.

• A higher leg threshold (2.5–3 MeV) would cut the recoil legs: not run.

Facility

• The TR-24 converter’s status and a port are unknown.

• No BNCT cyclotron has a fast port.

• Birmingham and MEDAPP reach further with softer beams.
